desc.he: החצר הפנימית, מקום העבודה. העזרה כולה מאה שמונים ושבע אמה על מאה שלושים וחמש: אחת עשרה אמה לעזרת כהנים, שלושים ושתיים למזבח, עשרים ושתיים בין המזבח לאולם, ומאה לבית. כאן מזבח העולה, הכיור ובית המטבחיים, ואש התמיד לא כבתה.
desc.en: The inner court where the service took place. The whole Azarah measured 187 by 135 amos: eleven for the Kohanim's court, thirty-two for the altar, twenty-two between the altar and the Ulam, and a hundred for the building. Here stood the outer altar, the laver and the slaughtering area, and the altar fire never went out.

desc.he: הפרוכת מבדילה בין ההיכל לקודש הקודשים. בבית שני היו שתי פרוכות ואמה ביניהן, מפני הספק במעמדה של אמה טרקסין. עוביה טפח, ארבעים אמה אורכה ועשרים רוחבה, ומשמונים ושתי ריבוא נעשית — לפי הברטנורא שמונים ושתי ריבוא דינרים, ויש מפרשים ששמונים ושתיים נערות ארגו אותה.
desc.en: The curtain dividing the Heichal from the Kodesh HaKodashim. In the Second Temple there were two curtains an amah apart because of the doubt over the status of the Amah Traksin. Each was a tefach thick, forty amos long and twenty wide, made at a cost of eighty-two ribo (820,000 dinars) — or, on another reading, by eighty-two maidens.

desc.en: The Ark of the Covenant: acacia overlaid with gold inside and out, two and a half amos long and one and a half wide and high, with two winged Keruvim facing each other on its cover; inside lay the Tablets. It was not in the Second Temple: it was hidden away in the days of King Yoshiyahu, and its place stood empty.

desc.en: Yachin, the southern of the two bronze pillars that Chiram cast for the entrance of Solomon's Ulam: eighteen amos tall with a five-amah capital. Its name means 'He will establish.' The pillars were broken up at the destruction of the First Temple, and Tractate Middot does not mention them in the Second.

desc.en: The Kohen Gadol's chamber, where he was secluded for the seven days before Yom Kippur. First called the chamber of the councillors, it was renamed Palhedrin after the royal officials replaced every year, once High Priests bought the office and rarely lasted longer. It required a mezuzah as a dwelling.

It was one of his two chambers, the other being Palhedrin on the south; the Gemara places this one on the north.

On either side it extended fifteen amos beyond the building as the Beis HaChalifos, where the slaughtering knives were kept.

geometry.notes: bayis_rishon: solid 1-amah wall x -10 .. 10, z -138 .. -139, 40 tall. bayis_sheni: no wall; two 20 x 40 curtains (see paroches) at z -138 and z -139, the outer one gathered on the south and the inner on the north (Mishnah Yoma 5:1).

desc.he: שני כרובים של עץ שמן מצופים זהב שעשה שלמה בקודש הקודשים, עשר אמות קומת כל אחד, וכנפיהם פרושות חמש אמות לכל כנף, כנף נוגעת בקיר וכנף נוגעת בכנף חברו. הארון הונח תחת כנפיהם. לא היו בבית שני.
desc.en: Two olive-wood cherubim overlaid with gold that Shlomo set in the Holy of Holies, each ten amos tall, their wings spread five amos each so that one wing touched the wall and the other met its fellow's. The Ark was placed beneath their wings. They were absent from the Second Temple.

position.note: standing in the Kodesh HaKodashim with the Ark beneath their wings (I Kings 8:6), spanning the 20-amah width; bayis_rishon only

views: toward the House, standing like a man (II Chronicles 3:13, Bava Batra 99a)
facing each other, turning apart when Israel did not do God's will (Bava Batra 99a)

questions.he: מה ההבדל בין כרובי הארון לכרובי שלמה?
questions.en: How did Shlomo's cherubim differ from those on the Ark?

questions.he: לאיזה כיוון פנו הכרובים?
questions.en: Which way did the cherubim face?

questions.he: מדוע לא היו כרובים בבית שני?
questions.en: Why were there no cherubim in the Second Temple?

geometry.notes: bayis_rishon only: two standing winged figures at x -5 and x 5, z -151, 10 tall, wings 5 each touching the side walls and each other above the Ark.
